analogy.title: A private think-tank for each word
analogy.text: After the words have chatted with each other in attention, each word steps into its own soundproof booth. Inside, it spreads its notes out over a much bigger desk (2048 slots instead of 512), crosses out anything negative, then condenses the useful bits back onto a 512-slot index card. Every booth has the same furniture and the same rules, so 'the', 'cat' and 'sat' are each processed identically and independently.

intro: We follow the three vectors for "the cat sat" as they enter the encoder's Feed Forward sub-layer, get expanded to 2048 dimensions, pass through ReLU, and are squeezed back to 512, exactly as in Eq. 2: FFN(x) = max(0, xW1 + b1)W2 + b2.

input.label: The normalized attention output for "the cat sat": one 512-dim vector per word

steps.title: Receive x
steps.what_happens: Each word's 512-dim vector from the Add & Norm after self-attention arrives, unchanged.
steps.narration: These vectors already mix in context from the other words via attention. The FFN will now transform each one on its own: the paper says it is applied "to each position separately and identically", so no information flows between 'the', 'cat' and 'sat' here.

views.caption: x entering the FFN (first 8 of 512 dims)

steps.title: Expand to d_ff = 2048
steps.what_happens: Each vector is multiplied by W1 (512×2048) and shifted by b1, making it four times wider.
steps.narration: The same W1 is used for all three words, which is why the paper also calls this a convolution with kernel size 1. Widening to d_ff = 2048 gives the layer room to compute many feature detectors per word; values can be positive or negative at this point.

steps.title: ReLU gate
steps.what_happens: Every negative number in the 2048-dim vectors is set to zero.
steps.narration: max(0, ·) is the only nonlinearity in the sub-layer; without it the two linear layers would collapse into one. Roughly half the inner features go silent per word, so each word lights up its own subset of detectors.

steps.title: Project back to d_model = 512
steps.what_happens: The active features are combined by W2 (2048×512) plus b2 into a 512-dim vector per word.
steps.narration: Every sub-layer must output d_model = 512 so the residual connection can add it to x. The result is a small, mostly modest-magnitude update vector for each word.

steps.title: FFN(x) leaves the block
steps.what_happens: The 512-dim update for each word exits the sub-layer.
steps.narration: Outside this block, dropout (P_drop = 0.1) is applied and the result goes to encoder_add_norm_2, which computes LayerNorm(x + FFN(x)). These weights are shared across positions but differ in each of the N = 6 encoder layers.

output.label: A 512-dim update vector per word, ready to be added back to x in encoder_add_norm_2

outro: Attention mixes information between words; the Feed Forward network then processes each word privately, expanding it from 512 to 2048 dims, applying ReLU, and projecting back to 512.
